correctness.rationale: For selected shore counts a,b and selected matched pairs c, the sum of assigned geodesic lengths is at most k(k-1)-ab+2c. This excludes fewer than n terminals and mixed n-terminal solutions. Odd shore constructions follow a near-one-factorization. For even n, the odd degree at each omitted opposite vertex prevents an n-terminal solution, while missing-to-missing edges require distinct selected matched-pair geodesics and exclude mixed (n+1)-terminal solutions. A near-one-factorization on n-1 vertices and a derangement construct every full-shore-plus-one optimizer. Exact enumeration independently reproduces optimum sizes/counts for 3<=n<=7, with all infinite claims proved symbolically.

A complete multipartite graph and a crown graph have distinct edge sets and shortest-path structure.

value.rationale: The result isolates a sharp odd-even response to perfect-matching deletion: the strong edge minimum drops by two on odd orders and not at all on even orders, relative to the established complete biclique result. It supplies a complete infinite-family classification and exact optimizer count, explained by near-one-factorizations and a missing-edge charging obstruction. This is a natural graph modification and structural statement rather than an arbitrary narrow census.
